label: thm:main
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:main}
The set $\mathfrak K$ is closed, connected, and completely invariant under
$F$, and $\pi|_{\mathfrak K}:\mathfrak K\to\mathbb C$ is proper. The set $\mathfrak K_{\mathcal M}$ is
compact and connected.
head: environment

label: thm:stable-main
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:stable-main}
Let $(c,z)\in\mathfrak K$. If $c\notin\mathcal M$, then $\mathfrak K$ is not locally
connected at $(c,z)$. If $c\in\mathcal M$ and $f_c$ is hyperbolic, then
$\mathfrak K$ is locally connected at $(c,z)$.
head: environment

label: thm:puzzle
title: Theorem
head: environment

label: thm:parabolic-main
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:parabolic-main}
There exist a primitive parabolic parameter $c_*\in\partial\mathcal M$ and
$z_*\in K_{c_*}\setminus J_{c_*}$ such that $\mathfrak K_{\mathcal M}$ is not locally
connected at $(c_*,z_*)$.
head: environment

label: thm:dimension-main
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:dimension-main}
For the boundary in $\mathbb C^2$ and the Euclidean metric,
\[
 \mathrm{H.dim}\,\partial\mathfrak K_{\mathcal M}=4.
\]
head: environment

label: lem:escape
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:escape}
For every $A\ge0$ there exists $R>0$ such that, for all $|c|\le A$,
\[
 K_c\subset\overline{D(0,R)},\qquad
 K_c=\bigcap_{k\ge0} f_c^{-k}\bigl(\overline{D(0,R)}\bigr).
\]
head: environment
name: Uniform escape radius

title: Proof
body_md:
Choose $R>2$ with $R^2-A>2R$. For $|c|\le A$ and $|w|\ge R$,
\[
 |f_c(w)|\ge |w|^2-A>2|w|.
\]
Consequently, $|f_c^k(z)|\ge R$ for some $k$ implies $z\notin K_c$.
Conversely, $|f_c^k(z)|\le R$ for every $k\ge0$ implies $z\in K_c$.
head: environment

label: lem:monotone
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:monotone}
Let $p:X\to B$ be a continuous surjection, where $X$ is compact and
$B$ is connected and Hausdorff. If $p^{-1}(\{b\})$ is connected
for every $b\in B$, then $X$ is connected.
head: environment
name: Connected fibers

title: Proof
body_md:
Suppose $X=A\sqcup D$ is a separation into nonempty open sets.
Both $A$ and $D$ are compact. Connectedness of each fiber gives
\[
 p(A)\cap p(D)=\varnothing,\qquad p(A)\cup p(D)=B.
\]
Since $B$ is Hausdorff, $p(A)$ and $p(D)$ are nonempty closed sets.
They therefore form a separation of $B$, a contradiction.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The complete invariance of $K_c$ under $f_c$ gives $F^{-1}(\mathfrak K)=\mathfrak K=F(\mathfrak K)$.

Let $(c_j,z_j)\in\mathfrak K$ with $(c_j,z_j)\to(c,z)$. Choose $A>0$ such that $|c|\leq A$ and $|c_j|\leq A$ for every $j$.
Let $R$ be given by Lemma~\ref{lem:escape}.
Continuity of $(c,z)\mapsto f_c^k(z)$ yields
\[
 |f_c^k(z)|=\lim_{j\to\infty}|f_{c_j}^k(z_j)|\le R
 \qquad(k\ge0).
\]
Thus $z\in K_c$, so $\mathfrak K$ is closed. 

If $B\subset\mathbb C$ is compact,
the same lemma gives a uniform $R$ such that
\[
 (\pi|_{\mathfrak K})^{-1}(B)=\mathfrak K_B
 \subset B\times\overline{D(0,R)}.
\]
The left-hand side is closed in the compact set on the right, proving
properness. Every $f_c$ has a fixed point in $K_c$, so
$\pi(\mathfrak K)=\mathbb C$.

Since $\pi|_{\mathfrak K}$ is proper and $\mathcal M$ is compact,
$
 \mathfrak K_{\mathcal M}=(\pi|_{\mathfrak K})^{-1}(\mathcal M)
$
is compact. The continuous surjection
$
 p=\pi|_{\mathfrak K_{\mathcal M}}:\mathfrak K_{\mathcal M}\to\mathcal M
$
has connected fibers $p^{-1}(\{c\})=\{c\}\times K_c$ for all
$c\in\mathcal M$. Lemma~\ref{lem:monotone} therefore implies that $\mathfrak K_{\mathcal M}$ is connected.

To prove that $\mathfrak K$ is connected, we attach each $\mathbf{x}\in\mathfrak K\setminus\mathfrak K_{\mathcal M}$ to $\mathfrak K_{\mathcal M}$ by a continuum. 
Write $\mathbf{x}=(c_0,z_0)$, choose $a\in\mathcal M$ with
$|c_0-a|=\operatorname{dist}(c_0,\mathcal M)=d>0$, and set
\[
 \gamma:[0,1]\to\mathbb C,\qquad
 \gamma(t)=(1-t)c_0+ta.
\]
Thus
$
 \gamma([0,1))\subset\mathbb C\setminus\mathcal M$ and $\gamma(1)=a\in\mathcal M.
$

For each $b\in\gamma([0,1))$, hyperbolic $J$-stability
\cite{MSS} gives a disk
$\mathcal U_b\Subset\mathbb C\setminus\mathcal M$ containing $b$ and a jointly
continuous holomorphic motion
\[
 h_b:\mathcal U_b\times J_b\to\mathbb C,
 \qquad h_b(b,\zeta)=\zeta,
\]
whose slices $h_b(c,\cdot):J_b\to J_c$ are homeomorphisms.
Whenever $\gamma([u,v])\subset\mathcal U_b$ and
$w\in J_{\gamma(u)}$, define
\begin{equation}\label{eq:local-transport}
 z(t)=h_b\!\left(\gamma(t),
    h_b(\gamma(u),\cdot)^{-1}(w)\right),\qquad t \in [u,v].
\end{equation}
Then $z(u)=w$ and $z(t)\in J_{\gamma(t)}$, and $z$ is continuous.

Set $t_k=1-2^{-k}$ for $k\ge0$. Each interval
$[t_k,t_{k+1}]$ admits a finite partition
$t_k=s_0<\cdots<s_\ell=t_{k+1}$ such that
$\gamma([s_{i-1},s_i])\subset\mathcal U_{b_i}$.
Starting from $z(0)=z_0\in K_{c_0}=J_{c_0}$, apply
\eqref{eq:local-transport} successively on these subintervals, with
$w=z(s_{i-1})$. The formulas agree at their endpoints and define
a continuous lift
\[
 L:[0,1)\to\mathfrak K,\qquad
 L(t)=(\gamma(t),z(t)),\qquad L(0)=\mathbf{x}.
\]
By properness,
$
 \mathfrak C:=\overline{L([0,1))}
 \subset\mathfrak K_{\gamma([0,1])}
$
is compact. It is connected because $L([0,1))$ is connected.
A subsequence of $L(t_k)$ converges to some $(a,w)\in\mathfrak C$;
since $a\in\mathcal M$, this limit lies in $\mathfrak C\cap\mathfrak K_{\mathcal M}$.

Only a cluster point of $L(t)$ as $t\to1$ is needed. Therefore
\[
 \mathfrak K=\mathfrak K_{\mathcal M}\cup
 \left(\bigcup_{\mathbf{x}\in\mathfrak K\setminus\mathfrak K_{\mathcal M}}\mathfrak C_{\mathbf{x}} \right),
 \qquad \mathfrak C_{\mathbf{x}}\cap\mathfrak K_{\mathcal M}\ne\varnothing,
\]
where each $\mathfrak C_{\mathbf{x}}$ is connected. Thus the union is connected.
head: environment

label: prop:stable-product
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:stable-product}
If $f_{c_0}$ is hyperbolic, there exist a disk $\mathcal U\ni c_0$
and a homeomorphism
\[
 T:\mathcal U\times K_{c_0}\to\mathfrak K_{\mathcal U}
\]
such that $\pi(T(c,z))=c$ and $T(c_0,z)=(c_0,z)$ for all
$(c,z)\in\mathcal U\times K_{c_0}$.
head: environment
name: Local product structure

title: Proof
body_md:
By $J$-stability \cite{MSS}, the Julia sets move holomorphically over
a sufficiently small disk $\mathcal U\ni c_0$. Adjoin the fixed
point $\infty$ and apply S\l{}odkowski's extension theorem
\cite{Slodkowski} (see also \cite[Theorem~3.1]{Roesch}).
The $\lambda$-lemma \cite[p.~193]{MSS} gives joint continuity
of the resulting holomorphic motion
\[
 h:\mathcal U\times\widehat\mathbb C\to\widehat\mathbb C,
 \qquad h^c(z):=h(c,z),
\]
normalized by $h^{c_0}=\operatorname{id}$, with each $h^c$ a sphere
homeomorphism fixing $\infty$ and satisfying $h^c(J_{c_0})=J_c$. 
It follows that $h^c(\mathbb C\setminus K_{c_0})=\mathbb C\setminus K_c$, and $ h^c(K_{c_0})=K_c$.
Thus $T:\mathcal U\times K_{c_0}\to\mathfrak K_{\mathcal U}$, defined by
$T(c,z)=(c,h^c(z))$, is a continuous bijection.
To verify continuity of $T^{-1}$, let $(c_j,w_j)\to(c,w)$ in
$\mathfrak K_{\mathcal U}$ and put $z_j=(h^{c_j})^{-1}(w_j)\in K_{c_0}$.
Every convergent subsequence $z_{j_k}\to z_*$ satisfies
\[
 h^c(z_*)=\lim_{k\to\infty}h^{c_{j_k}}(z_{j_k})=w,
\]
so $z_*=(h^c)^{-1}(w)$. Compactness of $K_{c_0}$ therefore gives
$z_j\to (h^c)^{-1}(w)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For $c_0\notin\mathcal M$, choose the disk $\mathcal{U}$ in
Proposition~\ref{prop:stable-product} inside $\mathbb C\setminus\mathcal M$.
Let $\pi_2:\mathcal U\times K_{c_0}\to K_{c_0}$ be the
second-coordinate projection. If $\mathfrak V\subset\mathfrak K_{\mathcal U}$
were a connected neighborhood of $(c_0,z)$, then
$\pi_2(T^{-1}(\mathfrak V))$ would be a connected subset of the
Cantor set $K_{c_0}$ and hence equal to $\{z\}$.
Thus $T^{-1}(\mathfrak V)\subset\mathcal U\times\{z\}$.
Since $K_{c_0}$ has no isolated points, this fiber has empty interior
in $\mathcal U\times K_{c_0}$, contradicting that
$T^{-1}(\mathfrak V)$ is a neighborhood.

For hyperbolic $c_0\in\mathcal M$, choose $\mathcal U$ inside its hyperbolic
component. Both $\mathcal U$ and $K_{c_0}$ are locally connected
\cite[Part II, Expos\'e X, Section 1]{DH}. Products of their open
connected neighborhoods form an open connected neighborhood basis
in $\mathcal U\times K_{c_0}$. In both cases,
$\mathfrak K_{\mathcal U}$ is open in $\mathfrak K$, so the homeomorphism $T$
transfers the asserted local properties to $\mathfrak K$.
head: environment

label: lem:puzzle-structure
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:puzzle-structure}
We have the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\textup{(i)}]  For $ 0\le m\le m'\le n $, we have
\[
 \mathfrak P_{n+1}\subset\mathfrak P_n,\qquad
 \mathfrak P_{n,m'}\subset\mathfrak P_{n,m}.
\]
\item[\textup{(ii)}] For every pair of integers $n\ge m\ge0$, the set
$\overline{\mathfrak P_{n,m}}$ is compact.
\item[\textup{(iii)}] For every $n\ge m\ge0$,
\[
 \pi(\overline{\mathfrak P_{n,m}})=\overline{\mathcal P_n},\qquad
 \overline{\mathfrak P_{n,m}}\cap(\{c_0\}\times\mathbb C)
 =\{c_0\}\times\overline{P_m}.
\]
\end{enumerate}
head: environment
name: Properties of mixed tubes

title: Proof
body_md:
\textup{(i)} The inclusions follow from planar nesting and
\eqref{eq:motion-compatibility}.

\textup{(ii)} The parameter pieces lie in the bounded set
$\mathcal P_0$, and the maximum principle gives $G_c(w)\le2^{-m}\le1$
on each tube. For bounded $c$, the escape estimate
$|f_c(w)|\ge |w|^2/2$ for large $|w|$ gives, by iteration,
$G_c(w)\ge\log(|w|/2)$. Thus $G_c(w)\to\infty$ uniformly as
$|w|\to\infty$, so the tubes are bounded in $\mathbb C^2$ and their
closures are compact.

\textup{(iii)}  Since
$\pi(\mathfrak P_{n,m})=\mathcal P_n$, we have $ \pi(\overline{\mathfrak P_{n,m}}) \subset\overline{\mathcal P_n} $.
By (ii), $\overline{\mathfrak P_{n,m}}$ is compact.
It follows that $\overline{\mathcal P_n} \subset\pi(\overline{\mathfrak P_{n,m}})$.
For the slice identity, let
\[
 (c_j,h_n^{c_j}(w_j))\to(c_0,w),
 \qquad c_j\in\mathcal P_n,\quad w_j\in P_m.
\]
A subsequence satisfies $w_j\to w_*\in\overline{P_m}$. Joint
continuity and $h_n^{c_0}=\operatorname{id}$ imply
$w=h_n^{c_0}(w_*)=w_*$. Conversely, approximating each
$w\in\overline{P_m}$ by points of $P_m$ at the fixed parameter
$c_0$ gives the reverse inclusion.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Choose a rational wake for the non-degenerate pair $(c_0,z_0)$. The critical-orbit assumption gives
$c_0\notin\mathcal I_n$ for
all $n$, so the parameter nest is defined. Graph avoidance gives
$z_0\in P_n$ for all $n$.
Suppose $\mathcal I(c_0)=\{c_0\}$ and $I_{c_0}(z_0)=\{z_0\}$.
The projection identity in Lemma~\ref{lem:puzzle-structure}\textup{(iii)}
gives $\pi(\mathfrak I(c_0,z_0))\subset\mathcal I(c_0)=\{c_0\}$.
Intersecting its central slice identities therefore yields
\[
 \mathfrak I(c_0,z_0)
 =\mathfrak I(c_0,z_0)\cap(\{c_0\}\times\mathbb C)
 =\{c_0\}\times I_{c_0}(z_0)=\{(c_0,z_0)\}.
\]

Conversely, assume $\mathfrak I(c_0,z_0)=\{(c_0,z_0)\}$.
For $c\in\mathcal I(c_0)$, the sets
$L_n(c):=\overline{\mathfrak P_n}\cap(\{c\}\times\mathbb C)$
are nonempty, compact, and nested by
Lemma~\ref{lem:puzzle-structure}. Thus
\[
 \varnothing\ne\bigcap_nL_n(c)
 =\mathfrak I(c_0,z_0)\cap(\{c\}\times\mathbb C),
\]
which forces $c=c_0$. Hence $\mathcal I(c_0)=\{c_0\}$.
Intersecting the central slice identities gives
\[
 \{c_0\}\times I_{c_0}(z_0)
 =\mathfrak I(c_0,z_0)\cap(\{c_0\}\times\mathbb C)
 =\{(c_0,z_0)\},
\]
so $I_{c_0}(z_0)=\{z_0\}$.
head: environment

label: prop:open-mixed
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:open-mixed}
Suppose $\mathcal I(c_0)=\{c_0\}$ and
$z_0\in J_{c_0}\setminus\bigcup_{j\ge0}I_j^{c_0}$.
For each $m\ge0$ and all sufficiently large $n\ge m$,
$\mathfrak P_{n,m}\cap\mathfrak K_{\mathcal M}$ is a connected relatively open
neighborhood of $(c_0,z_0)$ in $\mathfrak K_{\mathcal M}$.
head: environment
name: Open mixed neighborhoods

title: Proof
body_md:
Choose a repelling periodic point $q_0\in J_{c_0}\cap P_m$.
Since $\overline{\mathcal P_n}$ shrinks to $c_0$, the implicit
function theorem and joint continuity of the motion give, for all
sufficiently large $n$, a holomorphic continuation $q$ on
$\mathcal P_n$ with $q(c)\in J_c\cap h_m^c(P_m)$.
By \eqref{eq:motion-compatibility},
\[
 \mathfrak P_{n,m}\cap\mathfrak K_{\mathcal M}
 =\{(c,w):c\in\mathcal P_n\cap\mathcal M,\ w\in K_c\cap h_m^c(P_m)\}.
\]
The base $\mathcal P_n\cap\mathcal M$ is connected: parapuzzle pieces
cut $\mathcal M$ along finitely many rational ray pairs; see the connectedness
argument in \cite[proof of Proposition~3.5]{SchleicherFibers}.
Each fiber $K_c\cap h_m^c(P_m)$ is connected by planar puzzle
connectivity and meets the connected graph
$\{(c,q(c)):c\in\mathcal P_n\cap\mathcal M\}$. Their union is therefore
connected. Joint continuity of $(c,w)\mapsto(h_m^c)^{-1}(w)$
(which follows from joint continuity of $h_m$ and compactness of
$\widehat\mathbb C$) gives relative openness. Finally, the set contains
$(c_0,z_0)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For the non-degenerate pair $(c_0,z_0)$, assume
$\mathcal I(c_0)=\{c_0\}$ and $I_{c_0}(z_0)=\{z_0\}$.
First, $z_0\in J_{c_0}$. Otherwise $z_0$ lies in a bounded Fatou
component $U_0$. Since each puzzle graph avoids $U_0$,
$U_0\subset P_m\ (m\ge0),\  U_0\subset I_{c_0}(z_0)=\{z_0\}$,
a contradiction.

Let $U$ be a neighborhood of $(c_0,z_0)$ in $\mathfrak K_{\mathcal M}$. Choose
$\varepsilon>0$ such that
$\mathfrak K_{\mathcal M}\cap(D(c_0,\varepsilon)\times D(z_0,\varepsilon))\subset U$.
Dynamical shrinking gives $m$ with
$\overline{P_m}\subset D(z_0,\varepsilon)$. By joint continuity
of $h_m$, compactness of $\overline{P_m}$, and parameter shrinking,
for all sufficiently large $n\ge m$ we have
$\mathcal P_n\subset D(c_0,\varepsilon)$ and
$h_m^c(\overline{P_m})\subset D(z_0,\varepsilon)$ for every
$c\in\mathcal P_n$. Proposition~\ref{prop:open-mixed} then gives
a connected relatively open neighborhood
$\mathfrak P_{n,m}\cap\mathfrak K_{\mathcal M}\subset U$ of $(c_0,z_0)$.
This proves local connectedness of $\mathfrak K_{\mathcal M}$ at $(c_0,z_0)$.
head: environment

label: lem:gate
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:gate}
Let $(c,z_*)\in\mathfrak K_{\mathcal M}$. Suppose that $a_n,b_n\in\mathcal M$ and
$z_n\in K_{a_n}$ satisfy
\[
 (a_n,z_n)\to(c,z_*),\qquad b_n\to c,
\]
and that $b_n$ separates $c$ and $a_n$ for every $n\ge1$.
If there exist $\rho>0$ and $N\ge1$ such that
\[
 K_{b_n}\cap D(z_*,\rho)=\varnothing\qquad(n\ge N),
\]
then $\mathfrak K_{\mathcal M}$ is not locally connected at $(c,z_*)$.
head: environment
name: Gate criterion

title: Proof
body_md:
Suppose that $\mathfrak K_{\mathcal M}$ is locally connected at $p_*=(c,z_*)$.
There is a relatively open connected set $\mathfrak N\subset\mathfrak K_{\mathcal M}$ with
$p_*\in\mathfrak N\subset\mathfrak K_{\mathcal M}\cap\bigl(\mathbb C\times D(z_*,\rho)\bigr)$.
For all sufficiently large $n$, $(a_n,z_n)\in\mathfrak N$.
The set $\pi(\mathfrak N)$ is connected and contains $c,a_n$;
hence it contains $b_n$. Consequently,
\[
 \varnothing\ne
 \{w:(b_n,w)\in\mathfrak N\}
 \subset K_{b_n}\cap D(z_*,\rho),
\]
contrary to the hypothesis.
head: environment

label: lem:real-gate
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:real-gate}
Let $b\in(-2,1/4)$ be a real parabolic root whose two characteristic
parameter rays are nonreal. Then
\[
 x,y\in\mathcal M\cap\mathbb R,\quad x<b<y
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 b\text{ separates }x\text{ and }y\text{ in }\mathcal M.
\]
In particular, this holds for every real primitive root of period
greater than one.
head: environment
name: Real-root gate

title: Proof
body_md:
The characteristic rays $\mathcal R(t^-)$ and
$\mathcal R(t^+)$ landing at $b$ are complex conjugate
\cite[Theorem~3.1 and Corollary~5.4]{MilnorPortrait}. Since
$t^\pm\notin\{0,1/2\}$ and the parameter B\"ottcher coordinate
commutes with conjugation, neither open ray intersects $\mathbb R$.
Thus
$\Gamma=\mathcal R(t^-) \cup\{b,\infty\}\cup\mathcal R(t^+)$
is a Jordan curve in $\widehat\mathbb C$ satisfying
\[
 \Gamma\cap(\mathbb R\cup\{\infty\})=\{b,\infty\},
 \qquad \Gamma\cap\mathcal M=\{b\}.
\]
The intervals $(-\infty,b)$ and $(b,\infty)$ lie in opposite
components of $\widehat\mathbb C\setminus\Gamma$. A connected subset of
$\mathcal M\setminus\{b\}$ lies in one of these components, so it cannot
contain both $x$ and $y$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Set $c_*=-7/4$, the primitive period-three root
\cite[Section~3]{RojasYampolsky}, and choose the preceding sequences.
The lower-limit inclusion gives
$\operatorname{dist}(z_*,J_{c_k^{(1)}})\to0$. Choose $z_k\in J_{c_k^{(1)}}$
realizing this distance.
Since $L_{c_*}^{(2)}$ is compact, set
$d=\operatorname{dist}(z_*,L_{c_*}^{(2)})>0,\  \rho=d/2$.
If $K_{c_k^{(2)}}\cap D(z_*,\rho)\ne\varnothing$ for infinitely many $k$, there would be $k_j\to\infty$ and
$w_j\in K_{c_{k_j}^{(2)}}\cap D(z_*,\rho)$. After extraction,
$w_j\to w\in\overline{D(z_*,\rho)}$, whereas
\eqref{eq:lavaurs-limits} gives $w\in L_{c_*}^{(2)}$. Hence
$d\le|w-z_*|\le d/2$, a contradiction.

Recursively choose increasing indices $k_n,\ell_n$ such that
\[
 a_n=c_{k_n}^{(1)},\qquad b_n=c_{\ell_n}^{(2)},\qquad
 c_*<a_{n+1}<b_n<a_n.
\]
Then $a_n,b_n\to c_*$. Relabeling $z_{k_n}$ as $z_n$, we have
$z_n\in J_{a_n}$ and
\[
 (a_n,z_n)\to(c_*,z_*),\qquad
 K_{b_n}\cap D(z_*,\rho)=\varnothing
\]
for all sufficiently large $n$.
By Lemma~\ref{lem:real-gate}, $b_n$ separates $c_*$ and $a_n$.
Lemma~\ref{lem:gate} therefore gives non-local connectivity of
$\mathfrak K_{\mathcal M}$ at $(c_*,z_*)$.

The Mandelbrot set is locally connected at primitive parabolic
parameters \cite{TanParabolic,SchleicherFibers}. Since $f_{c_*}$ is
geometrically finite, $J_{c_*}$ and $K_{c_*}$ are locally connected
\cite{DH,MilnorBook}. Finally, \eqref{eq:zstar} gives
$z_*\in K_{c_*}\setminus J_{c_*}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
First,
$\mathfrak K_{\partial\mathcal M}\subset\partial\mathfrak K_{\mathcal M}$.
Indeed, if $(c,z)\in\mathfrak K_{\partial\mathcal M}$, choose
$c_j\in\mathbb C\setminus\mathcal M$ with $c_j\to c$. Then
$(c_j,z)\notin\mathfrak K_{\mathcal M},\ (c_j,z)\to(c,z)\in\mathfrak K_{\mathcal M}$,
and $\mathfrak K_{\mathcal M}$ is closed.

Fix an open $\mathcal U\subset\mathbb C$ meeting $\partial\mathcal M$ and
$0<s<2$. Choose
\[
 c_s\in\mathcal U\cap\mathcal V_s\cap\partial\mathcal M,
 \qquad
 \overline{D(c_s,r)}\subset\mathcal U\cap\mathcal V_s
\]
for some $r>0$. Set
$\mathcal A_s=\partial\mathcal M\cap\overline{D(c_s,r)},\  \mathfrak E_s=\mathfrak K_{\mathcal A_s}$.
The set $\mathcal A_s$ is compact, and Theorem A gives
\[
 2=\mathrm{H.dim}\,(\partial\mathcal M\cap D(c_s,r))
 \le\mathrm{H.dim}\,\mathcal A_s\le2.
\]
For every $c\in\mathcal A_s$,
\[
 \mathrm{H.dim}\,K_c\ge\mathrm{H.dim}\,J_c
 \ge\operatorname{hypdim}(f_c)>s.
\]
By the standard slicing inequality \cite[Theorem~2.1]{HeraKeletiMathe},
\[
 \mathrm{H.dim}\,\bigl(\mathfrak K_{\partial\mathcal M}
 \cap(\mathcal U\times\mathbb C)\bigr)
 \ge\mathrm{H.dim}\,\mathfrak E_s\ge\mathrm{H.dim}\,\mathcal A_s+s=2+s.
\]
Letting $s\nearrow2$ gives
\[
 \mathrm{H.dim}\,\bigl(\mathfrak K_{\partial\mathcal M}
 \cap(\mathcal U\times\mathbb C)\bigr)=4.
\]
Taking $\mathcal U=\mathbb C$, we conclude that
\[
 4=\mathrm{H.dim}\,\mathfrak K_{\partial\mathcal M}
 \le\mathrm{H.dim}\,\partial\mathfrak K_{\mathcal M}\le4.
\]
head: environment
